title: Steering of topological criticality in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via non-Hermitian substitutional impurities
authors: Juan A. Cañas, Guo-Qing Zhang, A. Martín-Ruiz
abstract: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. Our primary focus is the discovery of a deterministic mechanism to actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries by introducing site-dependent, non-reciprocal intracell and intercell hopping amplitudes. Specifically, breaking the internal structural symmetry of the non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point. This mechanism allows for the controlled expansion or compression of the topological phase strictly via local defect asymmetry. We validate this boundary displacement through finite-size scaling analysis. The extracted correlation length critical exponents ($ν\approx 1.455$ and $ν\approx 1.397$ for symmetric and asymmetric configurations, respectively) confirm a disorder-induced departure from the pristine SSH universality class, with the exponent diverging at high defect densities. We also report an impurity-induced real-to-complex spectral transition geometrically characterized by the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. Ultimately, our results establish how isolated non-Hermitian asymmetries cooperatively interact to deterministically shift macroscopic topological protection.
summary: This paper demonstrates a deterministic method to actively shift the topological phase boundaries in an SSH chain by introducing localized, non-Hermitian impurities with broken internal symmetry. By controlling the asymmetry of these defects, researchers can expand or compress the topological regime without relying on global disorder. The findings establish a powerful link between local structural asymmetry and macroscopic topological protection.
main_problem: The paper investigates how localized, non-Hermitian impurities can actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries of a pristine Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain.
main_result: Breaking the internal structural symmetry of non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point, allowing controlled manipulation of topological protection via local defect asymmetry.
method: The analysis employs finite-size scaling, real-space winding number calculations, and ensemble averaging over random impurity configurations to characterize the topological transitions.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional SSH chain Hamiltonian modified by non-Hermitian, non-reciprocal substitutional impurities confined to specific unit cells. The bulk of the chain remains perfectly Hermitian.
key_observables:
Topological phase boundaries, correlation length critical exponents ($
u$), Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE), and the real-to-complex spectral transition.
important_parameters: The concentration and asymmetry ($\gamma_i, \gamma_e$) of the non-Hermitian impurities are the key tuning parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the bulk of the chain remains perfectly Hermitian and translationally invariant, while the impurities introduce localized, non-reciprocal perturbations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the real energy spectra and spatial probability density profiles for single defects, showing how the impurity state shifts energy within the topological or trivial regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the non-Hermitian SSH model to analyzing single defects, then extending to finite concentrations, and finally using finite-size scaling and statistical methods to quantify the deterministic shift of the critical point.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism to engineer topological phases using engineered local asymmetries, which is highly relevant for designing synthetic quantum materials or controlling edge states in open quantum systems.
